transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-07-09 14:23 PDT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Grace Huang (Redwood SRE), Oliver Reyes (Atlas ML Eng), Priya Kapoor (Atlas Product), Samir Desai (Atlas Infra), Jenna Park (Atlas CTO)
---
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll keep it tight 45 minutes. quick roll call?
[00:06] Oliver: Oliver here.
[00:07] Priya: Priya.
[00:08] Samir: Samir.
[00:09] Jenna: Jenna.
[00:10] Maya: great, Liam and Grace are with me. objective today is to review the benchmark numbers vs your baseline provider and agree next steps for the 24 hour soak, and security follow up.
[00:20] Liam: I'll kick off with the numbers we ran earlier this week; disclaimer transcription: some host names got munged in the logs. so we ran two main scenarios: steady-state 50 concurrent requests (each ~512 token prompt with 128 token gen) and peak bursts at 200 concurrent. baseline provider numbers are what Atlas supplied last week.
[00:35] Liam: For steady-state, Redwood Dedicated with int8 quantization + dynamic batching at 80ms batch wait gave: p50 latency ~95ms, p95 ~220ms, throughput ~380 tokens/sec aggregate per GPU. Baseline: p50 ~160ms, p95 ~380ms, throughput ~210 tokens/sec.
[00:58] Oliver: wait can you repeat the p95 numbers? I think our spreadsheet had baseline p95 at 320ms not 380.
[01:03] Liam: yeah there's a mismatch — we pulled the baseline from the run Samir uploaded; looks like their run used cpu fallback for kv cache in some intervals, that's probably why p95 spikes. we'll share raw logs so you can correlate.
[01:15] Samir: correct, our baseline run used ModelServeX managed instance with autoscale and they had one node fall back during the burst, so KL cache warmed slowly. we missed that in the first pass.
[01:25] Priya: okay this is why seeing raw logs helps. what's the cost delta you saw?
[01:30] Maya: rough back-of-envelope: on the pilot config Redwood Dedicated int8 runs about 40% lower cost per 1M tokens compared to the baseline configuration used by Atlas, taking into account GPU utilization and request queuing. exact numbers in the sheet.
[01:45] Oliver: can you call out what config you used for the baseline so we can reconcile? instance types, batch size etc.
[01:50] Liam: baseline we used the Atlas-provided runbook: ModelServeX c5-style frontends, g4dn-like GPUs, batch size 16, no quantization, KV cache disabled for cross-request prefixes. Redwood run: a40 class or a100 equivalent, q8_int8 model, batch target 48 (dynamic), prefix KV cache enabled, and continuous batching window 30ms.
[02:12] Jenna: a few questions on security before we go deep on perf: will logs include PII? how are audit logs surfaced? we need SOC2 artifacts.
[02:20] Grace: brief answer: by default we redact PII in telemetry feeds for hosted, Dedicated can be configured to only ship aggregated metrics; we have SOC 2 Type II report and API for audit logs, and we can integrate with your KMS for key management. we'll put the security pack in the folder.
[02:35] Jenna: ok please share the SOC2 and network diagrams.
[02:38] Maya: noted, that's on the next steps.
[02:40] Liam: back to perf, during burst tests Redwood sustained 150 concurrent inferences across two GPUs with p95 at ~320ms whereas baseline degraded to p95 650ms with queueing; throughput difference was about 1.8x in favor of Redwood. That matches our expectation with dynamic batching + prefix cache.
[02:58] Oliver: what's the delta if we remove quantization? we need to be sure quality doesn't drop.
[03:03] Liam: good point — we ran unquantized runs: Redwood FP16 p95 was ~260ms, so quantization (q8) gave ~15% latency improvement and 20-25% throughput improvement for your workload, with negligible quality delta on our eval prompts. we'll include the eval prompt set outputs.
[03:20] Priya: how did you measure quality? rouge, bleu? we need to see examples.
[03:24] Liam: we used your golden prompt set and an automated metric plus manual spot checks; will attach human diff examples.
[03:30] Samir: network wise, if we go Dedicated in our VPC, can we keep all traffic internal?
[03:34] Grace: yes Dedicated supports private connectivity (VPC peering / private link), and we offer a private control plane or an on-prem bundle if you need airgapped. key wraps via your KMS supported. we'll map the network ports in the doc.
[03:48] Jenna: good. on reliability — what fallbacks are you proposing?
[03:52] Liam: we recommend policy-based routing: primary to Redwood Dedicated, fallback to hosted Redwood API or a cheaper variant model to preserve availability. automatic model variant fallback cuts latency spikes.
[04:05] Oliver: can you also add expected SLO numbers we can insert into our SLA?
[04:08] Maya: yes we'll propose SLO targets (p99 latency goals per route) in the follow up.
[04:12] Priya: any gotchas for burst pricing? we don't want surprises.
[04:15] Maya: Dedicated has burst capacity and predictable commits; we'll show cost scenarios: baseline commit, burst buffer, and overage rates.
[04:22] Samir: re: benchmark disparity, I'll re-run the baseline with the exact runbook you described and upload logs.
[04:27] Liam: thanks, that will help root cause. also note we saw one noisy neighbor effect on the baseline provider during their autoscale which we couldn't reproduce on Redwood Dedicated because of pinned capacity.
[04:40] Priya: ok timeline: we want the 24h soak next week and a security deep dive.
[04:45] Maya: proposed dates: security deep dive week of 7/14, 24h soak on 7/16. sound good?
[04:49] Jenna: yes.
[04:50] Oliver: yes.
[04:51] Maya: recap of action items and next steps... we'll send spreadsheet and raw logs, Liam will send config recipe, Samir will re-run baseline and share logs, Grace will schedule soak test and provide network diagram and SOC2 artifacts. pricing draft will be included.
[04:57] Priya: thanks all.
[04:58] Maya: thanks, we'll follow up in email with links. bye.
[05:00] [call ends]

Notes on transcription: occasional name misspellings (ModelServeX sometimes read as ModelServe ex), timestamps approximate, some filler removed for brevity.
